info.title: Sevitout API
info.description: REST API for Sevitout, a Severity Event (SEV) management system: open and track incidents, manage postmortems, and drive SEV lifecycle automation. This is the same API the web app, Slack bot, and AI plugins all consume — every feature is reachable through it.

get.summary:
ListPlugins returns the currently enabled AI plugins that
TriggerAction/StreamAction can route to. Unlike
ConfigService.ListAIPlugins (Admin-only, full record), this is readable
by any authenticated user and never includes credentials or handler
internals — just enough to populate a "run AI action" menu.

ListUserDirectory is a minimal org-wide "who is this person" lookup —
deliberately narrower than ConfigService.ListUsers (an Admin-only
user-management surface): open to any authenticated Viewer, and returns
only the fields needed to resolve a role assignment or a Slack invite
(docs/roadmap.md Phase 10a), never role/active-status/audit fields.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
query filters by a case-insensitive substring match against name or
email, for the role-assignment user picker's search box (§10c); empty
returns everyone. Mutually composable with ids below (both may be set,
though typical callers use one or the other).

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
ids, when non-empty, restricts the result to exactly these user IDs —
used for a batch resolve of already-known IDs (e.g. Slack auto-invite
resolving every assigned role's user in one call).

get.summary: WhoAmI returns the identity of the currently authenticated caller.

patch.summary:
UpdateMyIntegrationIdentities lets the caller manage their own
self-service integration identities (Slack user ID, GitHub username,
Jira account ID — docs/roadmap.md Phase 10a), used to widen Slack
auto-invite and default new tracker issues to the creating user. Unlike
UpdateSEV's sparse-patch convention, this is full-replace: all three
fields are sent on every call, and an empty string clears that field —
this endpoint only ever touches these three fields, so "empty = leave
alone" would make clearing one impossible.

get.summary:
ListEnabledIntegrations is a viewer-safe signal of which integration_types
currently have meaningful store-configured settings or credentials
(docs/roadmap.md Phase 11a) — used by the SEV detail page to hide an
integration-tied action (e.g. "Create Jira issue") when that integration
isn't configured, without exposing anything an Admin-only endpoint
wouldn't already consider safe to hand to any Viewer: no settings
values, no credentials_configured per type, just the list of enabled
types. Reflects store-configured integrations only — see this RPC's
response doc comment for the static-env-var-fallback limitation.

put.summary:
--- Escalation thresholds (docs/requirements.md §16, docs/roadmap.md
Phase 15) --- per-severity-level "alert if open > N minutes with no
Incident Commander assigned" configuration, scanned by cmd/server's
escalation scanner. Reads/writes floor exactly like RetentionConfig.

get.summary:
GetIntegrationCatalog returns the fixed, ordered field schema for every
integration_type this server recognizes (docs/roadmap.md Phase 9) — a
pure translation of internal/integrations/catalog.All with no store
access. It's the single source of truth the admin UI renders its
sidebar + schema-driven detail form from, and UpsertIntegrationConfig
validates incoming requests against the same catalog.

GetSlackBotCredential returns the decrypted "slack" integration
credential pair (bot_token/app_token) — the one deliberate exception to
"credentials are never returned by any RPC in this service" above. It
exists solely so cmd/slackbot (a separate process that only talks to
this API over gRPC, with no direct datastore/encryption-key access) can
pick up a datastore-configured Slack token without a restart; see
docs/roadmap.md Phase 8. Gated server-side to the specific slackbot
service account (SLACKBOT_SERVICE_EMAIL), not merely Admin+ — an
unrelated admin session must not be able to pull plaintext Slack tokens
through this call. Returns empty fields (not an error) when the "slack"
integration has no credentials configured, so callers can fall back to
their own static tokens.

put.summary:
UpsertIntegrationConfig creates or replaces the settings and credentials
for one integration type. Credentials are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) before
being written to storage and are never returned by any RPC in this
service — only whether credentials are currently configured. The
integration_type and every credential/settings key (and, for a select
field, its value) are validated against GetIntegrationCatalog's schema
before anything is written — see this RPC's handler doc comment.

parameters.name: integrationType
parameters.description:
integration_type: one of GetIntegrationCatalog's fixed set — e.g.
"slack", "pagerduty", "github", "jira", "monitoring". Any other value is
rejected.

get.summary:
ListLevelingCriteriaForServices is the batch lookup the SEV creation
form and postmortem page use: every configured row across a SEV's
(possibly multiple) affected services, at one severity level, no
reduction — see ServiceLevelingCriteriaStore.ListForServices. Spans
multiple services, so it sits at a top-level path rather than nested
under one service.

post.summary:
--- Notifications & Alerting (docs/requirements.md §16/§18.5,
docs/roadmap.md Phase 15) --- an admin-configured routing rule set:
"for org role X, on any of events Y, post to channel_type at
channel_target." A fixed broadcast route, not per-user/per-incident
personalization. Reads sit at the Viewer floor (same reasoning as
ServiceSLA/LevelingCriteria); mutations are Admin-only. Rules are
ID-identified (Create/Update/Delete by id), matching AIPlugin's shape
above — a rule covering several events can no longer be addressed by
its field values the way the original single-event design could.

TestNotificationConfig sends one real test message per event in the
request straight to its channel_type/channel_target — bypassing
ListForEvent's event/severity matching entirely, so it works equally
for an already-saved rule (pass its current field values) or a rule
still being drafted in the Add-rule form (id is never needed). Lets an
admin verify a Slack channel/email address and the underlying
integration actually work without waiting for a real SEV event.
Admin-only, like every other mutation here — it has the same
real-world side effect (a message lands in a real channel/inbox) as
Create/Update.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
TestNotificationConfigRequest carries the same fields as
CreateNotificationConfigRequest (no id — see the RPC's doc comment).

get.summary:
ListOnCallRotations is readable by any authenticated user (Viewer+) so
the UI can show who is currently on-call.

ListServices is readable by any authenticated user (Viewer+) since
services are referenced throughout the system (e.g. picking affected
services on a SEV).

delete.summary:
DeleteService permanently removes a service record. To retire a service
while preserving historical SEV references, prefer UpdateService with
active=false instead.

get.summary:
ListLevelingCriteria returns every configured severity row (0-4) for one
service — what the admin editor renders as its 4-row table.

--- Per-service SEV leveling criteria (docs/roadmap.md Phase 14) ---
free-text guidance for what qualifies as one severity level for one
service — purely advisory, never enforced or validated against. Reads
sit at the same Viewer floor as GetServiceSLA/ListServiceSLAs, since
this is exactly what the SEV creation form and postmortem page need for
any authenticated user opening or reviewing a SEV. Mutations are
Admin-only, matching UpsertServiceSLA/DeleteServiceSLA.

ListServiceSLAs returns every configured severity row (0-4) for one
service — what the admin editor renders as its 4-row table.

--- Per-service, per-severity-level SLA targets (docs/roadmap.md
Phase 12) --- readable by any authenticated user (Viewer+), same floor
as GetService/ListServices — the resolved numbers are already exposed to
any Viewer via SEVResponse.sla_status, so gating the raw config any
tighter would protect nothing. Mutations (Upsert/Delete) are Admin-only,
matching UpdateService/DeleteService.
ListUsers is Admin-only; the directory includes email addresses.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
query filters the directory by a case-insensitive substring match
against name or email; empty returns everyone.

get.summary:
GetServiceMetrics aggregates SEVs into per-(service, severity level)
rollups over a trailing window: SEV count, average MTTD/MTTM/MTTR, and
an SLA compliance breakdown (docs/roadmap.md Phase 13 — the aggregate
counterpart to Phase 12's per-SEV live sla_status on SEVResponse).

parameters.name: windowDays
parameters.description:
window_days is one of: 30, 60, 90, 180. Defaults to 30 when unset or 0
— validated in the handler, not here.

get.summary:
GetSEVTrends surfaces recurring failure patterns: SEVs sharing the same
affected service and root cause category (§17's "recurring incident
flag").

SearchSEVs returns SEVs matching the given filters, sorted and paginated.
query performs full-text search across a SEV's title, description, root
cause description, and business impact, plus any linked announcement.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: This is a request variable of the map type. The query format is "map_name[key]=value", e.g. If the map name is Age, the key type is string, and the value type is integer, the query parameter is expressed as Age["bob"]=18

get.summary:
ExportSEVs returns a filtered SEV list as CSV. The response is raw
text/csv bytes (google.api.HttpBody), not JSON — cmd/server/main.go
wraps the gateway's marshaler in runtime.HTTPBodyMarshaler, which
detects this response type and writes GetData() as the HTTP body with
GetContentType() as Content-Type instead of JSON-encoding it.

post.summary:
TriggerAction runs one AI action against a SEV and returns once the
provider responds; the result is also stored (ai_outputs) and broadcast
over WebSocket as an ai.output event, same as a proactive trigger.

get.summary:
ListOutputs returns previously generated AI output for a SEV, proactive
and user-triggered alike, oldest first.

parameters.name: audience
parameters.description: audience is an optional filter; omit to return all audiences

post.summary:
CreateGitHubIssue creates a new GitHub Issue pre-filled with SEV context,
links it to the SEV, and returns the linked task record.

CreateJiraIssue creates a new Jira issue pre-filled with SEV context,
links it to the SEV, and returns the linked task record.

JoinSlackChannel is a self-service "add me" action (docs/roadmap.md
Phase 11c) — unlike InviteRoleToSlack, it invites the *caller*, not a
named role holder, so it needs no role_id and no IC/Responder floor:
any Viewer with real (non visibility-restricted) access to the SEV may
call it. Resolution order is the caller's own identity: stored
SlackUserID, then LookupUserIDByEmail against the caller's own email.
FailedPrecondition when the SEV has no Slack channel recorded or the
caller has no resolvable Slack identity; PermissionDenied when the
caller lacks full access to a Sensitive SEV — see the handler's doc
comment for why that check is explicit here and wasn't part of Phase
10e's InviteRoleToSlack.

AssignRole, in addition to recording the assignment, best-effort invites
the role holder into the SEV's incident Slack channel when one is
already recorded (SEV.slack_channel_id) — every assigned role gets
added automatically, not just those present at channel-creation time
(docs/roadmap.md Phase 11 follow-up). A Slack-side failure here never
fails the assignment itself; InviteRoleToSlack below remains available
to retry or to invite a role assigned before the channel existed.

InviteRoleToSlack invites the person holding one role assignment into
the SEV's already-created incident Slack channel (docs/roadmap.md Phase
10e) — a manual "add to chat" action for a role assigned after the
channel was created (auto-invite at channel-creation time only covers
roles that existed at that moment). Fails FailedPrecondition when the
SEV has no Slack channel recorded, or when the role holder has no
resolvable Slack identity.

CreateShareLink is rejected for a Sensitive SEV (§14.1: "Sensitive SEVs
cannot have shareable links generated").

get.summary: ListTasks returns all tasks linked to a SEV.

post.summary: LinkTask links an existing external task (e.g. a GitHub Issue URL) to a SEV.

delete.summary: UnlinkTask removes a linked task from a SEV by its database ID.

patch.summary: UpdateTaskDueDate overrides the SLA-computed due date for a linked task.

parameters.name: relationshipType
parameters.description: relationship_type must be one of: related, caused-by, duplicate, recurrence-of

pluginId.description:
plugin_id selects which registered plugin to use. 0 (unset) uses the
first enabled plugin found — sufficient for v1, where orgs are expected
to configure at most one active plugin at a time.

audience.title: audience must be one of: internal, external, status-page

occurredAt.description: occurred_at is when the message was originally sent in the chat channel.

source.description: source identifies the chat platform (e.g., slack, email).

apiKey.description:
api_key, when non-empty, replaces the stored key; omit to keep the
existing one unchanged.

rateLimitPerMinute.description:
rate_limit_per_minute: unlike the response/create messages, 0 is a
meaningful value here (explicitly reset to unlimited), so this must be
wrapped to distinguish "not supplied" (nil) from "set to 0".

credentials.description:
credentials is write-only: encrypted with AES-256-GCM before storage.
Omit (leave empty) to keep the existing stored credentials unchanged
while updating settings.

mttdTargetSeconds.description:
A field left at 0 clears that metric's target (full-replace, like
UpdateRetentionConfigRequest — not a sparse patch).

toStatus.title: to_status must be one of: draft, in-review, approved

reason.description: reason is required and is written to the audit log.

unlockToken.description: unlock_token is required when the SEV is locked (PostmortemComplete status).

relationshipType.title: relationship_type must be one of: related, caused-by, duplicate, recurrence-of

unlockToken.description: unlock_token is required when the SEV is locked (PostmortemComplete status).
unlock_token is required when the SEV is locked (PostmortemComplete status).

slackChannelId.description:
slack_channel_id records the incident channel cmd/slackbot auto-created
for this SEV, written back right after channel creation (docs/roadmap.md
Phase 10e). Sparse-patch like every other field here: omitted on every
other UpdateSEV call, so this is safe to send from exactly one call site.

expiresInDays.description:
expires_in_days: how many days from now the link stays valid. Defaults
to 30 when unset or <= 0.

owner.description: owner is the GitHub organisation or user (e.g. "acme-corp").

body.description: body is the issue description; callers should pre-fill with SEV context.

priority.description: priority: critical | non-critical (controls default SLA due date).

assignee.description:
assignee is a GitHub login to assign the new issue to (wrapped into
GitHub's assignees: []string at the client layer). Optional — an empty
value creates the issue unassigned (docs/roadmap.md Phase 10f).

assigneeUserId.description:
assignee_user_id is the Sevitout user ID of the picked assignee, when
picked via the frontend's directory-backed AssigneePicker (as opposed
to a raw API call supplying only `assignee` directly) — the server
resolves it to that user's current display name and stores it as
TaskResponse.assignee_name, so the linked-tasks list can show a person's
name instead of their opaque GitHub login. Optional; a lookup failure
(e.g. an unrecognized ID) is non-fatal — issue creation still succeeds,
just without assignee_name set.

projectKey.description: project_key is the Jira project's key (e.g. "OPS"), not its numeric ID.

issueType.description:
issue_type is the target project's issue type name (e.g. "Task", "Bug")
— it must already exist on that project.

summary.description:
summary is the issue's title (Jira's naming for the field GitHub calls
"title").

description.description:
description is the issue body; callers should pre-fill with SEV
context.

priority.description: priority: critical | non-critical (controls default SLA due date).

assigneeAccountId.description:
assignee_account_id is a Jira Cloud account ID to assign the new issue
to (sent as Jira's assignee: {accountId: "..."}). Optional — an empty
value creates the issue unassigned. Unlike a GitHub login, this is an
opaque ID a user typically can't see in Jira's own UI without an
email->accountId lookup (docs/roadmap.md Phase 10f's documented UX risk).

assigneeUserId.description:
assignee_user_id is the Sevitout user ID of the picked assignee — same
meaning as CreateGitHubIssueRequest.assignee_user_id, resolved into
TaskResponse.assignee_name the same way.

priority.description: priority: critical | non-critical (controls default SLA due date).

dueDate.description: due_date overrides the computed SLA due date when provided.

contentType.description: The HTTP Content-Type header value specifying the content type of the body.

data.description: The HTTP request/response body as raw binary.

extensions.description:
Application specific response metadata. Must be set in the first response
for streaming APIs.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

v1AIAction.description:
AIAction enumerates the Provider methods a caller can invoke on demand
(§11.2) or that a lifecycle trigger invokes proactively (§11.1). Not every
action is meaningful for every trigger — see internal/ai.Dispatcher.

triggerEvent.description:
trigger_event is the lifecycle event that produced this output (e.g.
"sev.opened", "sev.mitigated", "sev.resolved", "postmortem.in_review"),
or "manual" for a TriggerAction/StreamAction call.

content.description:
content is plain text for narrative actions (Summarize,
DraftPostmortem, DraftAnnouncement) and JSON for structured, list-shaped
actions (SuggestRootCause, SuggestTasks, FindSimilar, SuggestResponders).
Always clearly labeled AI-generated wherever the UI renders it (§11).

rateLimitPerMinute.description: rate_limit_per_minute caps AI actions per minute for this plugin; 0 means unlimited.

audience.title: audience is one of: internal, external, status-page

key.description:
key is the storage key exactly as read/written by UpsertIntegrationConfig
(e.g. "bot_token", "cloud_id") — never itself shown to an admin; see label.

kind.description:
kind: "text" | "secret" | "select". "secret" fields are write-only
credentials, rendered password-masked; "select" fields must be one of
options.

required.description:
required is a UI-only affordance — see UpsertIntegrationConfig's doc
comment for why it isn't enforced server-side at upsert time.

options.description: options lists the valid values for a "select" field; empty otherwise.

v1CatalogField.description:
CatalogField describes one credential or settings key an integration_type
accepts — see internal/integrations/catalog.Field, which this mirrors
field-for-field.

apiKey.description:
api_key is write-only: encrypted with AES-256-GCM before storage, like
UpsertIntegrationConfigRequest.credentials.

manualUserId.description:
manual_user_id / manual_display_name plus a override_start/override_end
window define a manual override for a planned change; omit all four for
a normal PagerDuty-backed rotation.

id.description:
id is a caller-supplied slug (e.g. "checkout"); it is the stable
identifier referenced elsewhere (affected services, SLIs, on-call).

mttrTrends.description: mttr_trends always has exactly 3 entries: 7, 30, and 90-day windows.

postmortemCompletionRate.description:
postmortem_completion_rate is approved postmortems divided by total
postmortems, in [0, 1]. 0 when there are no postmortems yet.

slackUserId.description:
slack_user_id is included since resolving it is exactly why the Slack
auto-invite path calls this RPC — see docs/roadmap.md Phase 10d.

githubUsername.description:
github_username and jira_account_id back the GitHub/Jira issue-creation
assignee picker (docs/roadmap.md Phase 10f UX follow-up): the frontend
searches this directory and offers only users with the relevant field
set, displaying their name instead of the raw tracker-native ID.

integrations.description:
integrations is fixed-order — the order the admin UI's sidebar renders
in — matching internal/integrations/catalog.All exactly.

botToken.description:
bot_token / app_token are empty when the "slack" integration has no
datastore-configured credentials — not an error, since the caller has a
static-env-var fallback of its own.

credentialFields.description: credential_fields is empty for a settings-only integration (Monitoring).

v1IntegrationCatalogEntry.description:
IntegrationCatalogEntry describes one integration_type's complete field
schema — see internal/integrations/catalog.Integration.

credentialsConfigured.description:
credentials_configured is true when a non-empty credentials blob has
been stored; the decrypted value itself is never returned.

enabledTypes.description:
enabled_types lists the integration_types (e.g. "slack", "jira") that
currently have a meaningful store-configured credentials or settings
blob — the same "configured" concept the admin UI already uses (see
GetIntegrationCatalog). Known limitation: an integration activated only
via its static env-var fallback (PagerDuty/GitHub/Jira, with zero store
rows — see cmd/server's *Resolver types) is not reflected here, so it
shows as "not enabled" even though the backend would actually serve the
request. See docs/roadmap.md Phase 11a for why a fully accurate signal
is out of scope for this phase.

averageMttrSeconds.description:
average_mttr_seconds is the mean MTTRSeconds across SEVs resolved within
the last window_days days. 0 when no SEV resolved in that window.

events.description:
events is non-empty; a rule matches an incoming event when that event's
type appears anywhere in this list — one rule can cover several events
instead of requiring a separate rule per event.

maxSeverityLevel.description:
max_severity_level restricts this rule to SEVs at this severity level or
more critical (severity 1 is most critical); 0 means unset (every
severity), the same proto3 convention ServiceSLAResponse's target-seconds
fields already use.

hardDelete.description:
hard_delete controls what happens on expiry: false archives
(soft-delete), true purges permanently.

relationshipType.title: relationship_type is one of: related, caused-by, duplicate, recurrence-of

aiDisabled.description:
ai_disabled opts this SEV out of all AI plugin dispatch, proactive and
user-triggered (§11.3).

alertUrl.description:
alert_url links to the alert that fired (e.g. a PagerDuty incident or
Datadog monitor URL).

dashboardUrl.description:
dashboard_url links to the monitoring dashboard referenced by
monitoring_tool (§13.4).

snapshotUrl.description:
snapshot_url links to an already-hosted image of the monitoring chart at
detection time; rendered as an inline preview in the UI. No file upload
is supported — this is a URL to an image hosted elsewhere.

githubRepo.description:
github_repo is the "owner/repo" this SEV's code lives in (e.g.
"acme-corp/checkout-service"); pre-fills TaskService.CreateGitHubIssue's
owner/repo fields in the web UI. Set via UpdateSEV, not at creation.

rootCauseReferenceUrl.description:
root_cause_reference_url links to the concrete change that caused the
incident — e.g. a PR/commit diff or a config-management change —
alongside root_cause_category/root_cause_description's classification
and narrative. Set via UpdateSEV, not at creation.

query.description:
query is a saved query/expression (e.g. PromQL or a Datadog query
string) run against monitoring_tool — a separate concept from
dashboard_url, not a URL (§13.4).

slackChannelId.description:
slack_channel_id is the incident channel cmd/slackbot auto-created for
this SEV (§13.1, docs/roadmap.md Phase 10e) — absent for SEVs created
before this shipped, or whose channel-creation step never ran/failed.
Not sensitive (raw IDs are already exposed elsewhere), so it's on the
main response rather than gated.

slaStatus.description:
sla_status is this SEV's live SLA breach status (docs/roadmap.md
Phase 12), derived on every read against the most-strict SLA target
across its affected_services at severity_level — never trusted from
storage, the same discipline TaskResponse.overdue already applies to
task due dates. Absent (zero value) when no attached service has any
SLA target configured at this SEV's severity level.

rtpcSeconds.description:
rtpc_seconds is Resolution to Postmortem Complete
(postmortem_completed_at − resolved_at) — the same point-A-to-point-B
shape as dttm_seconds above, not "from started_at" like
mttd/mttm/mttr_seconds. Added as a Phase 12 follow-up SLA target for the
postmortem tail.

mttd.description:
Each status string is one of "ok", "at_risk", "breached",
"not_applicable" (internal/sev.SLAMetricStatus).

overall.description:
overall is the worst of mttd/mttm/mttr/rtpc — what a summary badge
should show.

mttdTargetSeconds.description:
The resolved target seconds per metric, 0 when not_applicable — so a UI
can show "target: 5m" alongside the status without a second lookup.

rtpc.description:
rtpc is Resolution to Postmortem Complete — measured from resolved_at,
not started_at like mttd/mttm/mttr above (see SEVResponse.rtpc_seconds).

v1SLAStatus.description:
SLAStatus is the live per-metric SLA breach status for one SEV, resolved
from the most-strict target across its affected services (see
ConfigService's ServiceSLA RPCs below for how targets are set).

avgMttdSeconds.description:
avg_mttd_seconds/avg_mttm_seconds/avg_mttr_seconds average only the
SEVs in this group with that metric already computed (nil-safe, same
discipline as MTTRTrend) — 0 when none have it yet.

slaOkCount.description:
sla_*_count bucket this group's SEVs by their live SLAEvaluation.Overall
(internal/sev/sla.go) — sla_not_applicable_count covers both "no SLA
configured for this service+severity" and "no baseline timestamp yet".

compliancePct.description:
compliance_pct is sla_ok_count / (sla_ok_count + sla_at_risk_count +
sla_breached_count), 0 when that denominator is 0 (every SEV in the
group is sla_not_applicable — not a real 0% compliance claim).

windowDays.description:
window_days echoes back the resolved window (after defaulting), same
defensive pattern MTTRTrend.window_days uses.

mttdTargetSeconds.description:
Target seconds per metric; 0 means unset (no SLA for that metric at this
severity level).

rtpcTargetSeconds.description:
rtpc_target_seconds targets Resolution to Postmortem Complete — see
SEVResponse.rtpc_seconds.

path.description:
path is the public view's URL path on this server — GET path needs no
authentication and returns the curated public SEV view.

taskId.description: task_id is the external identifier (e.g. "owner/repo#42" for GitHub Issues).

dueDate.description: due_date is null when the SEV has not yet been resolved.

assignee.description:
assignee is the tracker-native assignee identifier set at issue-creation
time (a GitHub login, or a Jira account ID) — see
CreateGitHubIssueRequest.assignee / CreateJiraIssueRequest.assignee_account_id
(docs/roadmap.md Phase 10f). Absent for tasks linked via LinkTask, or
created before this field existed.

assigneeName.description:
assignee_name is the Sevitout display name of the assignee, resolved
server-side at creation time from CreateGitHubIssueRequest.assignee_user_id
/ CreateJiraIssueRequest.assignee_user_id — a snapshot, not a live
lookup, the same trade-off already accepted for SEVRoleResponse's own
display_name. Absent when the assignee wasn't picked from Sevitout's
own directory (e.g. a raw API call supplying only the tracker-native
`assignee`); clients should fall back to `assignee` for display in that
case.

v1TaskResponse.description: TaskResponse is the linked task record returned by all TaskService RPCs.

v1TestNotificationConfigRequest.description:
TestNotificationConfigRequest carries the same fields as
CreateNotificationConfigRequest (no id — see the RPC's doc comment).

v1TestNotificationResult.description:
TestNotificationResult is one event's test-delivery outcome. error is
absent/empty on success.

unlockToken.description:
unlock_token is a short-lived JWT scoped to sev_id.
Pass it as unlock_token in subsequent mutation requests.

slackUserId.description:
slack_user_id, github_username, and jira_account_id mirror
WhoAmIResponse's self-service identity fields (docs/roadmap.md Phase
10a) — read-only here (AdminUsersPage shows, but never edits, another
user's identities; each user manages their own via /profile).

slack_user_id, github_username, and jira_account_id are the caller's
own self-service integration identities (docs/roadmap.md Phase 10a),
set via UpdateMyIntegrationIdentities.
